summary: Prepared the exact 0.2.1 remediation candidate on main@fea712a with a structural fix for the defective public 0.2.0 empty-shell incident. Both publishable packages are now exactly 0.2.1 (image-mind depends on @ran-sh/dsh-vision@^0.2.1; lockfile updated with zero unrelated churn). The release fail-safe is a content-hash prepack guard: each build records sha256 over its declared pack inputs into lib/.pack-state.json (scripts/pack-state.mjs, written by both build.mjs files), and scripts/pack-guard.mjs — wired as the npm `prepack` hook so BOTH `npm pack` and `npm publish` run it — rebuilds via the package's real build when outputs are missing or inputs changed, then verifies every required entry (vision: lib/index.js + lib/types/index.d.ts; image-mind: lib/index.js/lib/client.js/lib/cli.js) and fails closed before any tarball can be produced. Guard logs go to stderr so `npm pack --json` output stays machine-clean. Incident regression tests exercise the REAL npm packaging lifecycle on synthetic fixtures: auto-build ships working entries from a no-output state, hash-detected input changes repack fresh content, and a failing build aborts packaging with a clear error. Real 0.2.1 pack artifacts recorded: vision 15 files / 17.1 KB tgz; image-mind 9 files incl. lib/cli.js / 215.2 KB tgz — explicitly contrasting the defective public 0.2.0 (2 and 3 metadata-only files). Full gates green (ci/typecheck/build/test 360+65/test:package 13/test:built 6/git diff --check); publish dry-runs pass with complete file sets; read-only registry checks confirm both 0.2.1 versions absent and both broken 0.2.0 versions still present (shasums d43b1109/550b696f unchanged); local packed-artifact npx lifecycle acceptance vs exact rc.2 passes 9/9 including HTTP boot smoke, and PR-head CI run 32635184298 is green on all nine lanes with the guard executing in-lane. No registry write, tag, release or real-Harness touch occurred in this preparation stage.

tests.name: release-fail-safe-design-and-wiring
tests.evidence: Smallest robust mechanism chosen: npm's standard `prepack` lifecycle hook (runs automatically for BOTH `npm pack` and `npm publish`). Each build.mjs now ends by writing lib/.pack-state.json containing a sha256 CONTENT hash of the manifest-declared packGuard.inputs (src/** + build.mjs; content-based so fresh clones/checkouts are deterministic, unlike mtimes) via shared scripts/pack-state.mjs. scripts/pack-guard.mjs (prepack for both packages) compares current inputs hash + required entries against the state: fresh -> no-op; missing/stale -> runs the package's REAL build (`node build.mjs`, never a shortcut); post-build it verifies every declared entry exists and re-records state, exiting non-zero BEFORE npm can emit an incomplete tarball. Guard logs go to stderr so `npm pack --json` stdout stays valid JSON for tooling. State files are excluded by every files allowlist and never ship.

tests.name: incident-regression-through-real-packaging-lifecycle
tests.evidence: tests/pack-guard.test.ts drives actual `npm pack` against synthetic fixture packages wired to the same guard script: (1) no-output state -> pack succeeds WITH dist/hello.js present in the tarball and correct built content (auto-build path; exactly the 0.2.0 incident shape now impossible); (2) source edit without manual rebuild -> hash mismatch detected -> tarball carries FRESH content (no silent stale output); (3) failing build.mjs -> npm pack exits nonzero with 'pack-guard ... build failed ... refusing to package' and NO tarball entry (fail-closed). Live manual verification on the real vision package additionally showed: lib renamed away -> prepack logs 'rebuilding (required entries missing)' -> pack completes with all 15 files and lib restored.
